title: IV-VII: immediate and mediate creation
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): for God works in all things. But ye existence belonging toward things mediately created hangs no less out from God than belonging toward those immediately created; VII. God yet primarily acting — as plants, animals out from earth plus waters on ye following days — mediate stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which things stand as produced out from principles already created. VI. by means belonging toward ye sole nod belonging toward will, produces things — as heaven plus earth in ye beginning, angels, ye rational soul — immediate stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God without a creatures medium. And it stands as immediate or mediate. IV.
pass_b_english: IV. And it is immediate or mediate. Immediate is that by which God without a creatures medium, by the sole nod of will, produces things — as heaven and earth in the beginning, angels, the rational soul.
VI. Mediate is that by which things are produced from principles already created, God yet primarily acting — as plants, animals from earth and waters on the following days.
VII. But the existence of things mediately created hangs no less from God than of those immediately created; for God works in all things.
source_text: IV. Estque immediata aut mediata. Immediata est, qua Deus sine medio creaturae, solo nutu voluntatis, res producit — ut caelum et terra in principio, angeli, anima rationalis. VI. Mediata est, qua res e principiis jam creatis, Deo tamen primario agente, producuntur — ut plantae, animalia e terra et aquis diebus sequentibus. VII. Exsistentia vero rerum mediate creatarum non minus a Deo pendet quam immediate creatarum; Deus enim in omnibus operatur.
